title: Love the idea, buggy execution
body:
I love the app and how you can start a timer for each task. It really helps me stay focused and get things done.

However, the app is quite buggy. I’ve created multiple routines depending on my schedule. For context, I’m a medical student, so some days I study all day, while other days I have clinical rotations and then study afterward.

Even though the app allows you to switch between routines, it doesn’t stay on the selected one. When I reopen the app later in the day, it switches back to a default routine, even if I already completed tasks from that morning from a different routine. 

There are just too many bugs right now for me to rely on the app daily. I really wanted to purchase the lifetime membership, but it’s too buggy at the moment :(

title: Download it!
body: Life changing! I originally downloaded this app to build habits. Checking each habit I’ve completed feels so satisfying. It’s that small sense of pride that keeps you going. No matter how small that change seems, when you incorporate into your everyday life, it makes a difference. This app gives me an excuse to not skip out on small tasks from flossing to getting ahead of my assignments. The functions could be a bit smoother and the emoji keyboard has a small scrolling back-and-forth bug, but this app still does its job and completes its purpose well. The thing I love most about this app is how you can build a series of routines and have a timer for each of them. If you take too long, then the timer will turn red and begin to count your overtime. That has shown me when I surprisingly take too long on something that I didn’t think was a problem. Best of all, you have the option to make habits repeat between certain weekdays or a number of times a week, and if you do finish something that was a goal, you can mark it off forever. For example, when I got my braces off today, I could mark my habit of wearing elastics as forever completed. :) Something this app could change is seeing progress as “last 7 days” or “last 30 days” instead of “this week” or “this month”. Because when you just started a month, there’s not much to see with “this month,” and that forces me to scroll back to see my progress from last month, which is less efficient.

title: the app i’ve always wanted
body:
I’ve tried more than a few routine-building apps and this is by far the one closest to what I’ve always wanted in one of these. First of all— NO TIMER (or at least the option to turn it off.) Timers have always been a source of stress in my routines because I can’t always stick to whatever I’ve assigned a habit. Secondly— the LOOK! I’m a spreadsheet girl, plain and simple as that. The customization is always fun too. And finally— the routines themselves! I love that I can easily make weekly and daily habits and toggle between having them on specific days or just up to a certain # of times in a given time range.
My only gripe is that the app doesn’t keep my appearance preference (dark mode) when I access the app via a widget. I’m sure it’ll get addressed soon enough.
Anyway, this is well worth my money :) (written about a week into using it)

author: Saucyyy022

title: Clunky & counter-intuitive
body: Firstly, the way this app is organized doesn’t make sense to me. They call a “routine” any single task that repeats every day. A routine is a series of tasks that are repeated with some frequency, but you can’t create a grouping of tasks. The only way that you can group tasks is by the time of day that you want to do them. I like to check everything off on my watch and this is just impractical. When I went to bed last night, it only showed me the tasks from the morning, it didn’t show me any evening tasks and I didn’t want to see morning tasks in the evening. It also takes too long to tap off each item for your routine, because you have to go to through two screens on the watch in order to check off a simple item off your list
